questions.q:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

Despite his reluctance, she knew it was time to let I go and pursue his own dreams and aspirations.
o: to let I go and pursue his
questions.s:
The erroneous part is 'to let I go and pursue his'.

Key Points

  • The error in the sentence is the incorrect pronoun usage. The correct pronoun after "to let" should be in the objective case, "him," not the subjective case "I."
  • The corrected sentence should be: "Despite his reluctance, she knew it was time to let him go and pursue his own dreams and aspirations."
  • "Let" is a transitive verb that requires an object. In this context, "him" is the object of the verb "let." When the action of the verb is directed at oneself, the correct pronoun is in the objective case ("him"), not the subjective case ("I").
  • Here's another example:
    • Incorrect: "Despite his reluctance, Emily convinced he to move to Paris and chase his dream of becoming a chef."
    • Correct: "Despite his reluctance, Emily convinced him to move to Paris and chase his dream of becoming a chef."
  • In the corrected sentence, "him" is the objective form of the pronoun, matching the object position required by the verb "let."
  • Therefore, in the original sentence, "let I" should be corrected to "let him" for grammatical accuracy.

questions.q:
The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.

The official whom was in charge / of the investigation has been / transferred to a / different department last week.
o: The official whom was in charge
questions.s:
The error is the incorrect use of the relative pronoun "whom". The choice between "who" and "whom" depends on its grammatical role in the clause it introduces.

Who is a subject pronoun (it performs the verb's action).

Whom is an object pronoun (it receives the verb's action).

In the clause "...was in charge", the pronoun is the subject of the verb "was". We need a subject pronoun. Therefore, "who" is the correct choice.

Correct sentence:

The official who was in charge of the investigation has been transferred to a different department last week.

So, there is an error in the part mentioned in option a).

Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

Note:

Relative pronouns: A relative pronoun is used to connect a clause or phrase to a noun or pronoun. The clause modifies, or describes, the noun. The most common relative pronouns are who, whom, whose, which, and that. For example: She is the girl who received the award for bravery from our Home Minister.
